verse_text: One should save oneself by oneself; one should not lower oneself. For oneself is verily one's onw friend; oneself is verily one's own enemy.

sentence: Surrender then thy actions unto Me, live in Me, concentrate thine intellect on Me, and think always of Me [18.57].
verse_text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me and accepting Me as the supreme, have your mind ever fixed on Me by resorting to the concentration of your intellect.

sentence: It is suggested that you perform the actions that should be done without attachment to the results [3.19].
verse_text: Therefore, remaining unattached, always perform the obligatory duty, for, by performing (one's) duty without attachment, a person attains the Highest.

sentence: These actions should be performed while leaving aside the desire for rewards [18.6].
verse_text: But even these actions have to be undertaken by renouncing attachment and (hankering for) results. This is My firm and best conclusion, O Parhta.

verse_text: One's own duty, (though) defective, is superior to another's duty well performed. By performing a duty as dictated by one's own nature, one does not incur sin.

sentence: He who does his duty as his own nature reveals it, never sins [18.47].

verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: Right discrimination is not for the unsteady, and without concentration, there cannot be meditation, nor can there be peace [2.66].
verse_text: For the unsteady there is no wisdom, and there is no meditation for the unsteady man. And for an unmeditative man there is no peace. How can there be happiness for one without peace?

sentence: Knowledge is superior to blind action, meditation to mere knowledge, and renunciation of the fruit of action to meditation, for peace immediately follows renunciation [12.12].
verse_text: Knowledge is surely superior to practice; meditation surpasses knowledge. The renunciation of the results of works (excels) meditation. From renunciation, Peace follows immediately.

sentence: Excluding external objects, one may keep the gaze fixed between the eyebrows, with the inward and outward breathings passing equally through the nostrils [5.27].
verse_text: -5.28 Keeping the external objects outside, the eyes at the juncture of the eye-brows, and making eal the outgoing and incoming breaths that move through the nostrils, the contemplative who has control over his organs, mind and intellect should be fully intent on Liberation and free from desire, fear and anger. He who is ever is verily free.

sentence: The mind is fickle, turbulent, and as difficult to control as the wind [6.34].
verse_text: For, O Krsna, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong and obstinate. I consider its control to be as greatly difficult as of the wind.

sentence: Attachment and aversion for the objects of the senses abide in the senses, and one should not come under their sway [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Guided by pure reason, one may bravely restrain oneself by giving up attachment and hatred [18.51].
verse_text: Being endowed with a pure intellect, and controlling oneself with fortitude, rejecting the objects-beginning from sound [Sound, touch, form and colour, taste and smell.-Tr.], and eliminating attachment and hatred;

sentence: Little by little, by the help of reason controlled by fortitude, one may attain peace [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: He finds happiness in his own Self, and enjoys eternal bliss, whose heart does not yearn for the contacts of earth and whose Self is one with the Everlasting [5.21].
verse_text: With his heart unattached to external objects, he gets the bliss that is in the Self. With his heart absorbed in meditation on Brahman, he acires undecaying Bliss.

sentence: My actions do not fetter Me, nor do I desire anything that they can bring [4.14].
verse_text: Actions do not taint Me; for Me there is no hankering for the results of actions. One who knows Me thus, does not become bound by actions.

sentence: The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

verse_text: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

sentence: The joys that spring from external associations bring pain; they have their beginning and their endings [5.22].
verse_text: Since enjoyments that result from contact (with objects) are verily the sources of sorrow and have a beginning and an end, (therefore) O son of Kunti, the wise one does not delight in them.

sentence: The Spirit is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable, and knowing the Spirit as such, there is no cause to grieve [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: Coming unto the Divine, great souls go no more to the misery and death of earthly life, for they have gained perfection [8.15].
verse_text: As a result of reaching Me, the exalted ones who have attained the highest perfection do not get rirth which is an abode of sorrows and which is impermanent.

sentence: After many lives, the wise man realizes the Divine as it is, seeing that all is the innermost Self [7.19].
verse_text: At the end of many births the man of Knowledge attains Me, (realizing) that Vasudeva is all. Such a high-souled one is very rare.

sentence: For death is as sure for that which is born, as birth is for that which is dead, and therefore one should not grieve for what is inevitable [2.27].
verse_text: For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.

sentence: The Spirit in man is imperishable, and the Indweller in the body of everyone is ever indestructible [2.30].
verse_text: O descendant of Bharata, this embodied Self existing in everyone's body can never be killed. Therefore you ought not to grieve for all (these) beings.

sentence: It is named the Unmanifest, the Unthinkable, and the immutable, so knowing the Spirit as such, there is no cause to grieve [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality, which should be practised with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed [6.23].
verse_text: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

sentence: Just as the soul experiences infancy, youth, and old age within one body, it eventually passes into another [2.13].
verse_text: As are boyhood, youth and decrepitude to an embodied being in this (present) body, similar is the acisition of another body. This being so, an intelligent person does not get deluded.

sentence: The spirit is unborn, eternal, and ancient, and it does not die when the body is killed [2.20].
verse_text: Never is this One born, and never does It die; nor is it that having come to exist, It will again cease to be. This One is birthless, eternal, undecaying, ancient; It is not killed when the body is killed.

sentence: Death is as certain for the born as birth is for the dead [2.27].
verse_text: For death of anyone born is certain, and of the dead (re-) birth is a certainly. Therefore you ought not to grieve over an inevitable fact.

sentence: Beings are unmanifested in their beginning, manifested in their middle state, and unmanifested again in their end [2.28].
verse_text: O descendant of Bharata, all beings remain unmanifest in the beginning;; they become manifest in the middle. After death they certainly become unmanifest. What lamentation can there be with regard to them?

sentence: The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: Little by little, by the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of any other thing [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: And if you are not strong enough to practise concentration, then devote yourself to My service, do all your acts for My sake, and you shall still attain the goal [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Action for duty's sake is superior to inaction, as even the maintenance of the body would be impossible if one remained inactive [3.8].
verse_text: You perform the obligatory duties, for action is superior to inaction. And, through inaction, even the maintenance of your body will not be possible.

verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: If one is not strong enough to practice concentration, one may devote oneself to service and do all acts for the sake of the Divine [12.10].
verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Peace follows the renunciation of the fruits of actions [12.12].
verse_text: Knowledge is surely superior to practice; meditation surpasses knowledge. The renunciation of the results of works (excels) meditation. From renunciation, Peace follows immediately.

sentence: The mind is fickle, turbulent, obstinate, and extremely difficult to control, much like the wind [6.34].
verse_text: For, O Krsna, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong and obstinate. I consider its control to be as greatly difficult as of the wind.

sentence: When the mind follows the wandering senses, it carries away one's discrimination just as a ship at sea is tossed by a tempest [2.67].
verse_text: For, the mind which follows in the wake of the wandering senses, that (mind) carries away his wisdom like the mind (diverting) a boat on the waters.

sentence: Whenever the volatile and wavering mind wanders, one should restrain it and bring it back under the control of the Self [6.26].
verse_text: (The yogi) should bring (this mind) under the subjugation of the Self Itself, by restraining it from all those causes whatever due to which the restless, unsteady mind wanders away.

sentence: By using reason and fortitude, one can little by little attain peace and fix the mind on the Self [6.25].
verse_text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything whatsoever.

sentence: You have the right to work, but you have no right to the fruits of your labor [2.47].
verse_text: Your right is for action alone, never for the results. Do not become the agent of the results of action. May you not have any inclination for inaction.

verse_text: O Dhananjaya, indeed, action is ite inferior to the yoga of wisdom. Take resort to wisdom. Those who thirst for rewards are pitiable.

sentence: Renunciation is defined as the surrender of the fruits of all actions [18.2].
verse_text: The Blessed Lord said The learned ones know sannyasa to be the giving up of actions done with a desire for reward. The adepts call the abandonment of the results of all works as tyaga.

sentence: Peace follows immediately when one renounces the fruits of their actions [12.12].
verse_text: Knowledge is surely superior to practice; meditation surpasses knowledge. The renunciation of the results of works (excels) meditation. From renunciation, Peace follows immediately.

sentence: Having surrendered all claim to the results of his actions, always contented and independent, in reality he does nothing, even though he is apparently acting [4.20].
verse_text: Having given up attachment to the results of action, he who is ever-contented, dependent on nothing, he really does not do anything even though engaged in action.

sentence: Thus keeping his mind always in communion with Me, and with his thoughts subdued, he shall attain that Peace which is mine and which will lead him to liberation at last [6.15].
verse_text: Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

sentence: The Supreme Personality is declared to be the highest Purusha, transcending both the perishable and the imperishable [15.18].
verse_text: Since I am transcendental to the mutable and above even the immutable, hence I am well known in the world and in the Vedas as the supreme Person.

sentence: He who sees the Divine in everything and everything in the Divine is never separated from Him [6.30].
verse_text: One who sees Me in everything, and sees all things in Me-I do not out of his vision, and he also is not lost to My vision.

sentence: Through devotion, one knows the truth of who He is and enters into the Supreme [18.55].
verse_text: Through devotion he knows Me in reality, as to what and who I am. Then, having known Me in truth, he enters (into Me) immediately after that (Knowledge).

sentence: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: Surrender your actions unto the Divine, live in the Divine, concentrate your intellect on the Divine, and think always of the Divine [18.57].
verse_text: Mentally surrendering all actions to Me and accepting Me as the supreme, have your mind ever fixed on Me by resorting to the concentration of your intellect.

sentence: If you are unable to do even this, then seek refuge in union with the Divine, and with perfect self-control renounce the fruit of your action [12.11].
verse_text: If you are unable to do even this, in that case, having resorted to the Yoga for Me, thereafter renounce the results of all works by becoming controlled in mind.

verse_text: If you are unable even to practise, be intent on works for Me. By undertaking works for Me as well, you will attain perfection. [Identity with Brahman.]

sentence: Austerity performed for the sake of popularity or vanity comes from passion, and its result is always doubtful and temporary [17.18].
verse_text: That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honoured and worshipped, and also ostentatiously,-that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain and transitory.

sentence: Renunciation of action and the path of right action both lead to the highest, but of the two, right action is the better [5.2].
verse_text: The Blessed Lord said Both renunciation of actions and Karma-yoga lead to Liberation. Between the two, Karma-yoga, however, excels over renunciation of actions.

sentence: Those who keep their minds fixed on the Divine, worshipping with unwavering faith and concentration, are considered the best in yoga [12.2].
verse_text: The Blessed Lord said Those who meditate on Me by fixing their minds on Me with steadfast devotion (and) being endowed with supreme faith-they are considered to be the most perfect yogis according to Me.

sentence: Perhaps you could start by simply choosing a form of worship that feels natural to you, as the Divine makes that faith firm and unflinching [7.21].
verse_text: Whichever form (of a deity) any devotee wants to worship with faith, that very firm faith of his I strengthen.

sentence: The person who is full of faith and has their inner self merged in the Divine is deemed the most devout [6.47].
verse_text: Even among all the yogis, he who adores Me with his mind fixed on Me and with faith,he is considered by Me to be the best of the yogis.

sentence: By keeping the mind balanced and controlled, one attains the peace that abides in the Divine [6.15].
verse_text: Concentrating the mind thus for ever, the yogi of controlled mind achieves the Peace which culminates in Liberation and which abides in Me.

sentence: Even the wise are bewildered by the question of what constitutes action and inaction [4.16].
verse_text: Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

sentence: The language of these choices can sometimes perplex our reason and make us feel uncertain [3.2].
verse_text: You bewilder my understanding, as it were, by a seemingly conflicting statement! Tell me for certain one of these by which I may attain the highest Good.

sentence: It is said that the level reached by wisdom is also attained through right action, and he who sees these two as one knows the truth [5.5].
verse_text: The State [Sthana (State) is used in the derivative sense of 'the place in which one remains established, and from which one does not become relegated'.] that is reached by the Sankhyas, that is reached by the yogis as well. He sees who sees Sankhya and yoga as one.

sentence: Those who are truly established in one path obtain the fruits of both [5.4].
verse_text: The fools, not the learned ones, speak of Sankhya (the path of Knowledge) and (Karma-) yoga as different. Any one who properly resorts to even one (of them) gets the result of both.

sentence: The Self is described as unmanifested, unthinkable, and unchangeable [2.25].
verse_text: It is said that This is unmanifest; This is inconceivable; This is unchangeable. Therefore, having known This thus, you ougth not to grieve.

sentence: Constant yearning for the knowledge of the Self and pondering over the lessons of the great Truth is declared to be knowledge [13.12].
verse_text: Steadfastness in the knowledge of the Self, contemplation on the Goal of the knowledge of Reality-this is spoken of as Knowledge. Ignorance is that which is other than this.

sentence: One may learn this by prostrating, questioning, and serving those who have realized the Truth [4.34].
verse_text: Know that through prostration, iniry and service. The wise ones who have realized the Truth will impart the Knowledge to you.

sentence: Even the wise are sometimes bewildered when trying to distinguish between what constitutes action and what constitutes inaction [4.16].
verse_text: Even the intelligent are confounded as to what is action and what is inaction. I shall tell you of that action by knowing which you will become free from evil.

sentence: It is said that the senses are powerful, but beyond the senses is the mind, beyond the mind is the intellect, and beyond and greater than intellect is He [3.42].
verse_text: They say that the organs are superior (to the gross body); the mind is superior to the organs; but the intellect is superior to the mind. However, the one who is superior to the intellect is He.

sentence: Those deluded by the qualities of nature are attached to the functions of those qualities [3.29].
verse_text: Those who are wholly deluded by the gunas of Nature become attached to the activities of the gunas. The knower of the All should not disturb those of dull intellect, who do not know the All.

sentence: The ignorant do not see that it is He who is present in life or that it is He who enjoys pleasure through the qualities, as only the eye of wisdom sees [15.10].
verse_text: Persons who are diversely deluded do not see it even when it is leaving or residing (in this body), or experiencing, or in association with the alities. Those with the eye of knowledge see.

sentence: Restraining them all, let him meditate steadfastly on Me; for who thus conquers his senses achieves perfection [2.61].
verse_text: Controlling all of them, one should remain concentrated on Me as the supreme. For, the wisdom of one whose organs are under control becomes steadfast.

verse_text: Being endowed with a pure intellect, and controlling oneself with fortitude, rejecting the objects-beginning from sound [Sound, touch, form and colour, taste and smell.-Tr.], and eliminating attachment and hatred;

sentence: Harmlessness, truth, absence of anger, renunciation, peacefulness, absence of crookedness, compassion towards beings, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and absence of fickleness are qualities to consider [16.2].
verse_text: Non-injury, truthfulness, absence of anger, renunciation, control of the internal organ, absence of vilification, kindness to creatures, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, freedom from restlessness;

sentence: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality, and it should be practised with determination and with a heart which refuses to be depressed [6.23].
verse_text: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga has to be practised with perservance and with an undepressed heart.

sentence: When a man dwells on the objects of sense, he creates an attraction for them; attraction develops into desire, and desire breeds anger [2.62].
verse_text: -2.63 In the case of a person who dwells on objects, there arises attachment for them. From attachment grows hankering, from hankering springs anger.

sentence: The love and hate which are aroused by the objects of sense arise from Nature; do not yield to them [3.34].
verse_text: Attraction and repulsion are ordained with regard to the objects of all the organs. One should not come under the sway of these two, because they are his adversaries.

sentence: One who is equal to friends and enemies, who is equipoised in honor and dishonor, heat and cold, happiness and distress, who is free from attachment and remains steady in situations of gain or loss [12.18].
To him who has conquered his lower nature by Its help, the Self is a friend, but to him who has not done so, It is an enemy [6.6].
verse_text: Of him, by whom has been conered his very self by the self, his self is the friend of his self. But, for one who has not conered his self, his self itself acts inimically like an enemy.

sentence: Perform all your actions with your mind concentrated on the Divine, renouncing attachment and looking upon success and failure with an equal eye [2.48].
verse_text: By being established in Yoga, O Dhananjaya (Arjuna), undertake actions, casting off attachment and remaining eipoised in success and failure. Eanimity is called Yoga.

sentence: In this world, people are fettered by action unless it is performed as a sacrifice, so let your acts be done without attachment, as sacrifice only [3.9].
verse_text: This man becomes bound by actions other than that action meant for God. Without being attached, O son of Kunti, you perform actions for Him.

sentence: These actions should be performed leaving aside attachment and the desire for rewards [18.6].
verse_text: But even these actions have to be undertaken by renouncing attachment and (hankering for) results. This is My firm and best conclusion, O Parhta.
